question.title: Will the fuel loading of the Palisades Nuclear Generating Station's reactor core be completed before December 16, 2026?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: Will Palisades finish loading its reactor core before Dec 16, 2026?**

**1. Current status (as of Nov 26, 2026): undecided. I found no announcement that loading is complete.**
- **Aug 30, 2026:** Palisades entered Mode 6 and began loading its 204 assemblies. Eight of the 204 were in the vessel by Aug 31. Holtec's spokesperson would not say when loading would finish.
- **Sept 21:** Holtec said one assembly tilted after it was placed and the grapple was disengaged, and loading remained paused.
- **Oct 21:** Holtec recovered the tilted assembly with a purpose-built Fuel Movement Device and moved it to the spent fuel pool. Holtec said workers can now resume fuel loading. The NRC and Holtec are still investigating why the assembly tipped.
- **Oct 29–30:** Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the plant "would be back running before the end of this year." He said "We hope at the end in November, but it is very close." Holtec has not publicly confirmed that date. The same ENR article notes a media report that restart is about a year behind schedule and that Holtec cut hundreds of workers. Holtec did not confirm this report.
- **Oct 29 (WMUK):** "fuel assemblies were reloaded into the reactor earlier this month." This is loosely worded and conflicts with Holtec's own Oct 21 statement that loading was only then resuming.
- **Nov 19 (Michigan Public):** "nuclear fuel has been loaded into its reactors, but it is not generating power." This is ambiguous. It may mean full core load or just that some fuel is in the vessel.
- **Holtec's sequence:** Holtec expects the plant to move to cold shutdown (Mode 5) once fuel loading is completed and the reactor vessel is reassembled. A Mode 5 announcement would be strong evidence that loading is done.
- **Not found:** a Holtec or NRC statement saying all 204 assemblies are loaded. I also found no loading-percentage update after Oct 21.
- **Caveat:** the question was posed on Nov 26. That suggests loading was not publicly confirmed complete by then, but this is inference. It is possible loading finished quietly without a press release.

**2. Resolution source:** The question names Holtec and the NRC as "credible sources". The latest Holtec primary item I found is the Oct 21 recovery update, which says loading would resume. The "Progress Report on Palisades' March to Startup" page I saw still says loading is paused. That page is undated in the snippet and appears to be the Sept 21 version. I did not find a Holtec release in November. The NRC's Palisades pages may carry event or inspection notices, but I did not check them.

**3. Base rate and timing**
- Only 8 of 204 assemblies were reported loaded in the first day or so. A normal PWR core load takes roughly a few days to a week or two. This is general industry knowledge, not from the sources above.
- If the pace holds, completion would take days after resumption, not weeks. Loading was cleared to resume Oct 21, and by Nov 26 it has been about 5 weeks. That is ample time unless new issues arose.
- This restart has slipped repeatedly, from late 2025 to early 2026 to late 2026, and loading itself was delayed by roughly 7 weeks.
- There is no true base rate for restarts of decommissioned US reactors, because Palisades is the first.

**4. Scheduled or possible events before Dec 16**
- Wright's "end of November" restart hope is a public benchmark. A restart cannot happen before loading is complete, and the reactor vessel must also be reassembled.
- ENR noted that Holtec must submit something to the NRC by "Nov." (the snippet is cut off). It is likely related to the safety-culture or fuel-event follow-up.
- Holtec said the NRC's root-cause review of the tilted assembly is ongoing.
- Holtec posts progress reports, and news outlets such as WMUK, Michigan Public and ANS follow them closely. Any Mode 5 or "fuel load complete" announcement would likely be reported quickly.
- Holtec's S-1 IPO filings (the last one was cited as FY2026) state fuel loading "has commenced". The final S-1/A text may update on completion.
- Holtec's contractual power-delivery deadline is March 2027.

**5. Markets and forecasters:** I found no prediction-market prices or forecaster numbers for this question or for the Palisades restart.

**6. Evidence on each side**

*Toward Yes:*
- The blocking assembly was removed Oct 21, and Holtec said loading would resume.
- Michigan Public (Nov 19) says fuel "has been loaded".
- Wright is publicly pushing for restart by about Nov 30. A restart on that timeline would require loading to be complete before Dec 16.
- Core loading is normally quick.
- Holtec's S-1/A says it is "on track" to restart in 2026.

*Toward No / uncertainty:*
- No explicit completion announcement has been found in the five weeks since resumption.
- Holtec has declined to give timelines, and prior timelines slipped.
- A media report says the restart is about a year behind. Holtec did not confirm it.
- Open issues include the root-cause investigation, the NRC's "chilled work environment" finding, and workforce cuts.
- The pace of loading after Oct 21 is unknown.
- The resolution is ambiguous if the milestone was completed before the question window, since it requires completion "before Dec 16". Completion on any earlier date should still count.

slots.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 20 days. The question closes December 16, 2026, and today is November 26.

(b) Status quo: Loading began August 30, paused in September after an assembly tilted, and was cleared to resume on October 21. No Holtec or NRC statement confirms that all 204 assemblies are loaded, and the question itself says the criteria are not yet met. If nothing changes, this resolves No.

(c) No scenario: Loading resumed slowly or not at all after October 21, held up by the unfinished root-cause investigation of the tilted assembly, NRC scrutiny, workforce cuts, or a new problem. Holtec continues to give no timeline, and no completion or cold-shutdown (Mode 5) announcement appears before December 16.

(d) Yes scenario: Loading did resume in late October and is finished or nearly so. Holtec or the NRC confirms full core load or entry into Mode 5 in late November or early December, consistent with Energy Secretary Wright's push for restart by year-end.

Rationale:

- **For Yes:** The physical blocker was removed on October 21. A normal core load takes days to a couple of weeks, so five weeks was ample time. Media reports from October 29 and November 19 loosely say fuel "has been loaded". Wright publicly targeted restart by the end of November or the end of the year, and Holtec has a strong incentive to hit a 2026 restart.
- **For No:** Holtec publicised the start of loading and the assembly recovery, so it would very likely have announced completion. Five weeks without one suggests loading is not finished, and may be going slowly or be paused again. The project has slipped repeatedly, and loading itself was delayed about seven weeks. The question was written on the premise that completion has not occurred. Only about 20 days remain.

The speed of a normal core load and the political pressure roughly offset the silence since October 21 and the project's history of delays, so I land slightly below even, leaning toward the status quo.

Probability: 42%

(a) Time left: about 20 days, from Nov 26 to the Dec 16, 2026 cutoff. A Holtec or NRC statement confirming completion would likely be picked up by trade press within days of the event.

(b) Status quo: Loading began Aug 30, stalled for about seven weeks over a tilted assembly, and was cleared to resume Oct 21. No explicit statement that all 204 assemblies are loaded has been found, and the question says the criteria are not yet met. If nothing changes, meaning no completion announcement, the question resolves No.

(c) No scenario: Loading did not actually resume quickly after Oct 21, for example because Holtec or the NRC wanted the root-cause review of the tipped assembly finished first, or because of new equipment or procedural problems, or staffing cuts. Loading is then still incomplete or unconfirmed on Dec 16. This project has slipped repeatedly, and Holtec refuses to give timelines.

(d) Yes scenario: Loading resumed in late October or November and proceeds at a normal pace, which is days to a couple of weeks for a pressurised-water reactor core. Holtec then announces completion or entry into cold shutdown before Dec 16. Alternatively, loading is already essentially done, as the Nov 19 Michigan Public wording hints, and a confirming statement appears.

Rationale: The physical task is short. Even at the slow initial pace of about 8 assemblies a day, 204 assemblies take under four weeks, and by Dec 16 there will have been eight weeks since the obstacle was cleared. Energy Secretary Wright's late-October comment that restart was "very close" and the news reports that fuel "has been loaded" both suggest substantial progress.

Against that, there has been no explicit completion announcement in five weeks, even though Holtec normally publicises milestones. That silence, plus the question's statement that criteria are unmet, suggests loading was slower or later to resume than hoped. The root-cause investigation is still open, the NRC has flagged a chilled work environment, and this project has a consistent record of delay. Confirmation by a credible source is also required, which adds a small reporting risk.

On balance I lean modestly toward Yes, tempered by the status quo and the unexplained silence.

Probability: 62%

## OUTSIDE VIEW

**Reference class:** Two candidates apply.
1. Core loads at a PWR once they have started. These normally finish in days to about two weeks. After an interruption is cleared, nearly all finish within a few weeks.
2. Milestones in first-of-a-kind nuclear projects with a record of slipping (Vogtle, and Palisades itself). Palisades' restart slipped from late 2025 to early 2026 to late 2026, and the fuel load itself stalled for about seven weeks. Near-term milestones in such projects miss their stated dates perhaps 40–60% of the time.

**Base rate:** A plant that began loading 3 months before the deadline, with its known blocker removed 8 weeks before it, would finish in time roughly 80–85% of the time on the first reference class. The slippage record of the second pulls that down.

**Outside-view forecast:** about 70%.

## INSIDE VIEW

**(a) Time left:** About 20 days, to Dec 15, 2026. Completion at any earlier date should also count.

**(b) Status quo:** Loading began Aug 30, paused in September over a tilted assembly, and was cleared to resume Oct 21. There is no confirmed completion. If nothing changed and loading was still paused or unannounced, this resolves No. If loading is under way, the default path is completion within days.

**(c) No scenario:** Loading did not really resume at pace after Oct 21. The NRC root-cause review, the "chilled work environment" finding, workforce cuts or a second fuel-handling problem kept loading slow or stopped. Holtec then stays quiet through mid-December, or finishes later in December or in early 2027, ahead of its March 2027 contractual deadline.

**(d) Yes scenario:** Loading resumed in late October and either finished quietly in November or finishes in early December. Holtec or the NRC then confirms that all 204 assemblies are loaded or that the plant has moved to Mode 5.

**Evidence adjustments:**
- **Blocker removed Oct 21 (moderately up):** Holtec said loading could resume, which leaves about 8 weeks for a task that takes 1–2 weeks.
- **Energy Secretary Wright's comment, Oct 29–30 (slightly up):** He said restart was "very close" and hoped for end of November. This implies insiders expected loading to finish soon, but political statements on this project have been optimistic before.
- **Michigan Public (Nov 19) and WMUK (Oct 29) wording (slightly up):** Both say fuel "has been loaded" or "reloaded". The wording is loose but consistent with completion or near-completion.
- **No completion announcement in 5 weeks (moderately down):** Holtec publicised the start of loading and the recovery of the assembly, so silence on completion suggests either slow progress or another hold.
- **Question framing (down):** The question was created Nov 26 and states the criteria are not yet met.
- **Open issues (slightly down):** Holtec declines to give timelines, the root-cause review is still open, and there are reports of the project running a year behind with staffing cuts.
- **Resolution risk (slightly down):** A quiet completion might lack a clear credible-source statement by the deadline.

Taken together, the physical task is short and the obstacle was removed, but five weeks of silence after the go-ahead on a project with chronic slippage is a real warning sign. That puts me slightly below the outside view.

Probability: 62%

**(a) Time left:** About 20 days, from Nov 26 to Dec 16, 2026. Any "fuel load complete" or Mode 5 announcement would be reported quickly by Holtec, the NRC and local outlets (WMUK, Michigan Public, ANS).

**(b) Status quo:** No public confirmation that all 204 assemblies are loaded. The last primary-source statement (Holtec, Oct 21) says loading can resume after the tilted assembly was recovered. Strictly, the status quo is "not yet confirmed." But the underlying process has had about five weeks to run, and a normal PWR core load takes days to two weeks.

**(c) No scenario:** Loading did not actually resume in earnest after Oct 21. Holtec or the NRC may have waited for the root-cause analysis of the tilted assembly, or for corrective actions such as procedure or equipment changes, or for the safety-culture ("chilled work environment") follow-up. Workforce cuts or a new fuel-handling problem could have slowed progress further. Holtec also stays quiet, so no credible source confirms completion before Dec 16.

**(d) Yes scenario:** Loading resumed in late October and finished within a couple of weeks. That fits Michigan Public's Nov 19 statement that fuel "has been loaded" and Secretary Wright's push for a late-November or end-of-year restart. Holtec then announces Mode 5 or fuel-load completion, or this is confirmed in NRC documents or the S-1/A, before Dec 16. Completion before the question opened should still count, since the criterion is only "completed before December 16."

**Rationale:**
- **For Yes:**
  - The physical bottleneck, the tilted assembly, was removed five weeks ago, and Holtec explicitly said loading could resume.
  - Core loading is mechanically quick.
  - The Energy Secretary, who presumably has insider information, said on Oct 29 that restart was "very close" and possibly by end of November. That requires loading to be done.
  - A Nov 19 report says fuel has been loaded.
- **For No:**
  - No explicit Holtec or NRC completion statement has surfaced.
  - The question was posed on Nov 26, which hints that completion wasn't obviously public.
  - The project has slipped repeatedly.
  - Holtec has avoided giving dates.
  - The resolution depends on a credible source confirming completion, so Holtec's communication habits add risk.
- **Overall:** Weighting the status quo appropriately (a slow, delay-prone project), I still lean Yes, because both the physical timeline and the secondary reporting point to completion either already having happened or happening within the window.

Probability: 70%

**(a) Time left:** About 20 days, from Nov 26 to Dec 16, 2026. Holtec, the NRC and local media (WMUK, Michigan Public, ANS) report Palisades milestones quickly, so the outcome should be clear within that window.

**(b) Status quo:** Loading was cleared to resume on Oct 21. No public confirmation of full core load (204/204 assemblies) or of entry into Mode 5 has been found. If nothing changed, the question would resolve No. But the underlying process is not frozen. The blocker was removed five weeks ago, and loading a full pressurized-water-reactor core normally takes days to about two weeks. The status quo is therefore "loading in progress or quietly finished," not "stalled."

**(c) No scenario:** The NRC's root-cause review of the tilted assembly turns up something systemic. Possibilities include bowed assemblies, a lower-core-plate or alignment problem, or a procedural or safety-culture issue tied to the "chilled work environment" finding. Holtec then holds or slows loading, perhaps adding inspections of each assembly or waiting for NRC sign-off. Workforce cuts and the reported one-year schedule slip compound the delay. Holtec stays quiet, and no completion announcement appears before Dec 16.

**(d) Yes scenario:** Loading resumed in late October or November and has finished or soon finishes. This fits Michigan Public's Nov 19 report that fuel "has been loaded" and Secretary Wright's "very close" remark. Holtec or the NRC then confirms completion or announces Mode 5 after the reactor vessel is reassembled, before Dec 16. A completion that happened earlier but is documented later should also count.

**Rationale:**
- **For Yes:**
  - The physical task is short.
  - The blocking obstacle was removed more than a month ago.
  - Holtec has a strong commercial incentive: an IPO, a March 2027 power-delivery deadline, and a "restart in 2026" claim.
  - Federal political pressure supports a fast restart.
  - One local outlet already describes fuel as loaded.
- **For No:**
  - There has been no explicit completion statement in five weeks, which is odd if loading took only days. That suggests either a further hold, or that completion simply wasn't publicized.
  - This restart has slipped repeatedly.
  - The open root-cause investigation could impose conditions.
  - The question being posed on Nov 26 implies the milestone had not been clearly confirmed.

Weighing the short physical timeline and strong incentives against the conspicuous silence and Holtec's history of slips, I lean Yes, but with meaningful risk.

Probability: 64%

(a) About 20 days remain until Dec 16, 2026.

(b) The status quo is that loading is not publicly confirmed complete, so the question stays No unless a completion announcement appears. However, the status quo is also that loading resumed on Oct 21. At normal pace, a core load takes days, so it has probably been done for some time.

(c) No scenario: loading resumed slowly or stopped again because of new problems. Examples are another tilted assembly, NRC investigation findings, workforce cuts, or a slow pace. Completion then slips past Dec 16. Another No path is that loading finished but there is no credible public confirmation. A strict resolver could then resolve No, though the milestone would still have been reached.

(d) Yes scenario: workers resumed loading after Oct 21 and finished all 204 assemblies in late October or November. Holtec then reassembled the vessel and moved to Mode 5, and Wright's "end of November" restart hope is partly borne out. Michigan Public's Nov 19 line that fuel "has been loaded" supports this. Holtec or the NRC would confirm it in a progress report.

Weighing the evidence:
- Five weeks have passed since resumption, which is ample time for a core load of about 204 assemblies.
- Wright said on Oct 29–30 that restart was very close. That implies loading was complete or nearly so.
- The question was created Nov 26, which suggests completion was not widely confirmed by then. Question generators often build questions from articles that state a milestone as upcoming, so this is weak evidence.

I estimate about a 75% chance that loading is completed and confirmed by Dec 16.

Probability: 76%

(a) Time left: about 20 days, until December 15, 2026. A Holtec or NRC confirmation could come at any point, or may already exist unnoticed.

(b) Status quo: loading began August 30, paused in September after an assembly tilted, and was cleared to resume on October 21. No explicit "all 204 assemblies loaded" statement has been found. If nothing changes in the public record, the question resolves No, although the physical work may be nearly or fully done.

(c) No scenario: loading did not really resume at pace after October 21, because of the NRC root-cause review of the tilted assembly, further fuel-handling problems, the chilled-work-environment finding or workforce cuts. Completion then slips into late December or 2027, as earlier milestones on this project repeatedly have, or no clear statement of completion appears before December 16.

(d) Yes scenario: loading resumed in late October and, at a normal PWR pace of one to two weeks for a full core, finished in November or finishes in early December. Holtec or the NRC then confirms it, most likely through a "fuel load complete" or Mode 5 announcement, consistent with the Energy Secretary's push for restart by year-end.

Rationale: The evidence leans Yes.

- **Obstacle removed:** the tilted assembly was recovered on October 21, and Holtec said loading could resume.
- **Ample time:** core loading normally takes days to a couple of weeks, and five weeks have already passed with three more to go.
- **Supporting reports:** Michigan Public said on November 19 that fuel "has been loaded," and Energy Secretary Wright said in late October that restart was "very close," hoping for end of November. Both suggest loading is complete or nearly so, though the Michigan Public wording is ambiguous.

Against that, several things hold me back from going higher.

- **No confirmation:** I found no explicit completion statement from Holtec or the NRC, and the question itself says the criteria have not yet been met.
- **Track record:** this restart has slipped repeatedly, and Holtec has declined to give a timeline for finishing the load.
- **Open issues:** the root-cause investigation is still ongoing, and the pace of loading since October 21 is unknown.

Probability: 73%
